newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine strike turnout "low" says minister.
newsitem.headline: Argentine strike turnout "low" says minister.

text.p: Argentina's Defense Minister Jorge Dominguez said there was 50 percent less turnout for Thursday's strike than during the last strike in September.
"The turnout is 50 percent less than in the last stoppage," Dominguez said, according to state news agency Telam.
The minister added that "the information we have received indicates the turnout is low." Dominguez made his comments after the end of the weekly government cabinet meeting.
"It (the strike) is already a success," Rodolfo Daer, the head of Argentina's main CGT labor federation, told local radio earlier Thursday. "There are more buses in the streets than people."
The government said that only 40 percent of buses and 30 percent of trains were running in Buenos Aires. The city's subway was running at 70 percent.

The walkout, the third general strike this year, was called by unions to protest three decrees on labor market reforms signed by President Carlos Menem last week. Unlike the other strikes however, no marches nor protests were called for this time.
A 36-hour strike in September had a 90 percent turnout according to unions, although the government said it was less effective.
